label: Fictional sample data
evaluationSummary: Reevaluation 2025-05 (fictional results): rating scales from teacher and family show clinically significant externalizing behavior at school. WISC-V Full Scale IQ 95. WIAT-4 Reading Comprehension 88, Math Problem Solving 84. Functional Behavior Assessment completed August 2026 (see BIP).
strengths: Sneezy is artistic, helps younger students, and responds well to adults he trusts. He is motivated by drawing time and classroom jobs.
needs: Coping when frustrated, starting non-preferred tasks, solving conflicts with peers, multi-digit multiplication.
parentConcerns: His family wants fewer calls home and for him to have a good relationship with his teachers and classmates.
disabilityImpact: Outbursts during difficult academic tasks and peer conflicts interrupt his learning and others' learning. He needs explicit instruction in coping and problem-solving skills, plus a structured behavior plan.

presentLevels.text: ABC data (2 weeks, Aug-Sep 2026): verbal outbursts (yelling, pushing materials off the desk) average 4 a day, mostly within 3 minutes of being given a non-preferred written task. Uses a coping strategy independently in 1 of 5 opportunities.
Starts non-preferred tasks within 2 minutes of directions on 35% of occasions.
Uses a conflict-resolution step with peers in 1 of 5 observed conflicts.
Reads grade 3 text at benchmark; written responses are short.
Multi-digit multiplication 40% accuracy; facts are fluent.

transition.note: Not required: the student is in elementary school (Georgia requires a transition plan by 9th grade entry or age 16).

goals.baseline: Uses a coping strategy independently in 1 of 5 opportunities.
goals.statement: When frustrated, Sneezy will use a taught coping strategy (break request, breathing, cool-down area) in 4 of 5 observed opportunities for 4 consecutive weeks.

objectives.statement: With a visual prompt, Sneezy will choose a coping strategy from his card in 4 of 5 opportunities.
Sneezy will return from the cool-down area within 5 minutes in 4 of 5 uses.

goals.statement: Sneezy will reduce verbal outbursts to 1 or fewer per day for 4 consecutive weeks.
goals.criteriaForMastery: 1 or fewer per day, 4 consecutive weeks

objectives.statement: Sneezy will have 2 or fewer outbursts per day for 2 consecutive weeks.

goals.baseline: Starts non-preferred tasks within 2 minutes on 35% of occasions.
goals.statement: Given a first/then board and a choice of task order, Sneezy will start non-preferred tasks within 2 minutes of directions on 80% of occasions across 3 weeks.

objectives.statement: Sneezy will start the first item with an adult check-in on 70% of occasions.

goals.baseline: Uses a conflict-resolution step in 1 of 5 conflicts.
goals.statement: Sneezy will use the 4-step conflict-resolution routine with a peer, with no more than one adult prompt, in 4 of 5 observed conflicts.

objectives.statement: Sneezy will name the problem and his feelings in 4 of 5 role-plays.

goals.statement: Sneezy will solve 2-digit by 2-digit multiplication problems with 80% accuracy across 3 consecutive probes.

objectives.statement: Sneezy will solve 2-digit by 1-digit problems with 85% accuracy.

lreExplanation: Sneezy attends a separate special education school through a district placement because he needs a therapeutic setting with embedded behavior support throughout the day.

esy.notes: Data from last summer show significant regression in coping skills with slow recoupment. ESY: 2 sessions a week for 4 weeks in June 2027.

targetBehaviors.name: Verbal outburst
targetBehaviors.operationalDefinition: Yelling above conversational volume and/or pushing materials off the desk, lasting at least 5 seconds.
targetBehaviors.baseline: Average 4 a day (10 school days, Aug-Sep 2026)

behaviorPlan.settingEvents: Mornings after a difficult bus ride; days with a substitute.
behaviorPlan.antecedents: Non-preferred written tasks (especially math and writing); peer teasing.
behaviorPlan.consequences: Task removed or delayed; adult attention and conversation.
behaviorPlan.functionStatement: When given a difficult written task, Sneezy has an outburst to escape the task; adult attention is a secondary function.
replacementBehaviors: Request a break or help using words or a card
Use the cool-down area for up to 5 minutes
behaviorPlan.antecedentStrategies: Chunk tasks; offer choice of order; first/then board; pre-correct before writing tasks; check-in at arrival.
behaviorPlan.teachingStrategies: Daily coping-skills practice with RBT; weekly counseling group; role-play conflict resolution.
behaviorPlan.reinforcement: Points for task starts and coping-strategy use, exchanged for drawing time or a classroom job; behavior-specific praise.
behaviorPlan.responseStrategies: Calm, neutral prompt to his coping card; task stays but is reduced; planned ignoring of yelling; praise as soon as he re-engages.
behaviorPlan.crisisPlan: If behavior becomes unsafe, classmates move to a safe area with one adult, and two trained staff follow the school's de-escalation procedure. The family is informed the same day.

dataCollection.method: Daily frequency count, latency recording and ABC notes

team.note: General curriculum representative (the school has no general education classrooms)
